name: Site B — CitiHardware and neighboring highway junction

source.projection: local equirectangular, metres; study area only
assumptions: Provisional OSM corridor, not field validated

Carriageways, median, islands, openings and stop lines are estimated from the owner's overhead imagery (scale bar; imagery dated 2025-05-03) and Street View (June-July 2026); check every size in the field
Service lanes, concrete strips, aprons, sheds, street lights and buildings are drawn only: no simulated traffic uses them
The median and islands are not engine obstacles; lanes and turn paths are placed around them and acceptance counts any vehicle contact
Owner-confirmed access rule (2026-11-07): buses and trucks are prohibited on Sobrecarey Street in both directions; this is local knowledge, not independently verified signage or a cited ordinance

Bonifacio stays open to buses and trucks. The simulation keeps them in the kerb lane on the highway approach from the northeast so their tail clears the median during the turn. Confirm real lane use in the field
No U-turns are simulated at the mid-block median gaps, and their zebras and stop lines are paint only
The yellow box markings in the 2025 imagery are not drawn: the 2026 Street View shows no yellow, pending confirmation
Beyond the imagery (more than about 175 m southwest of the study junction) the same layout is assumed
Dao and Acacia continue straight past the imagery, leaving out their OSM far bends, so their far alignment and end points are approximate
Only CitiHardware is a candidate signal/RL junction
Neighboring junction uses first-come no-signal control
Synthetic demand; no traffic effectiveness claimed

Side streets (D45) are provisional geometry from OpenStreetMap, painted and approved by the owner, not field-checked: Sobrecarey, Bonifacio and Osmeña Streets north to Magsaysay Street, Magsaysay Street, the west loop (Doctor Juan Gonzales Avenue and two unnamed streets), Dao Street on to Ebony Street, the loop back to the highway through the median opening, and the inner link to Acacia Street
Map bends under 5 m are drawn straight, the first 30 m at each end of a new street is drawn straight, and bends are circular arcs of 25 m radius
New streets are unnamed and one lane each way; they join the highway on its median centre line, where the carriageways bend to the junction inside its stop lines
Every new junction uses first-come right-of-way, and Site B stays the only signal and RL candidate
Pedestrians cross only at the study junction and the neighbouring junction, as before; people crossing the new streets are not modelled

Generated traffic starts and ends only at the boundaries of the highway, Sobrecarey Street and Dao Street; side streets carry traffic only when route choice detours it (they cost three times their driving time)
Sobrecarey and Dao Streets run 60 m past the grid to boundaries, so the counted traffic still enters them; the streets the owner did not paint beyond the grid are not modelled
Acacia Street ends at the inner link, so the Acacia and Bonifacio boundaries of the earlier layout are gone; the earlier layout is kept as a listed revision
The highway runs 80 m past the Osmeña junction; its pavement strips and median there are drawn only

supplement.reason: Magsaysay Street and the north ends of Sobrecarey, Bonifacio and Osmeña Streets lie beyond the first extract
